subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She has been feeling__ unwell__ lately, so she decided to take a break and rest.
solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2 ('Under the weather')**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Under the weather"** refers to feeling unwell, sick, or not in good health. (अस्वस्थ महसूस करना) • **Example:** I didn’t go to work today because I’ve been feeling under the weather. • The phrase is commonly used to describe a temporary state of poor health or fatigue. (थोड़े समय के लिए स्वास्थ्य खराब होना या थकावट) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 ('Under the weather')**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Under the radar** (नजर से बचकर): Refers to doing something secretly or without attracting attention. • **Example:** The new startup is operating under the radar until they are ready to launch officially. • **Under the sun** (संसार में): Refers to everything that exists or is possible in the world. • **Example:** They discussed every topic under the sun during their meeting. • **Under pressure** (दबाव में): Refers to a state of being stressed or forced to do something due to external demands. • **Example:** She performs well under pressure, which is why she excels in stressful situations. 36:T990, The correct answer is: **Irritable**.
